document_title: Software on the radio. Merlin's account of the Project Nexus kickoff
_note: Slide strings read off the render report's text nodes and each frame's own source line by build_copy.py.
caption:
Did software work the radio?

Merlin says TxDOT invited it to the Project Nexus kickoff at Fort Worth Alliance Airport on September 10th. It says its Merlin Pilot demonstrated AI-powered air traffic control communications. TxDOT's and the FAA's releases skip Merlin.

TxDOT's first phase tests helicopters and fixed-wing planes. Its first flights carry no passengers and collect data and validate routes. Medical and cargo logistics come next. The FAA says it will write rules from that data.

Counted from September 10th, October 8th is 28 days into the three years TxDOT gives Project Nexus.

Only Merlin's release names its Caravan, and only in a photo caption. None of the three releases says whether a pilot was aboard or prints a measured result. Is silence in all three the whole public record on both?

#ProjectNexus #TxDOT #FortWorth

S1.headline: Software on the radio
S1.body: Merlin says it demonstrated AI-powered air traffic control communications at TxDOT's Project Nexus kickoff on September 10th. Neither TxDOT's release nor the FAA's names Merlin. The plane is drawn to illustrate.
strings: Merlin says it demonstrated AI-powered air traffic control communications at TxDOT's Project Nexus kickoff on September 10th. Neither TxDOT's release nor the FAA's names Merlin. The plane is drawn to illustrate.

S2.headline: Phase one began here
S2.body: The Texas Department of Transportation launched the first phase of Project Nexus at Fort Worth Alliance Airport, as part of a federal pilot program for new aircraft. The FAA called it the first Texas demonstration under the program. The tower and the radio path are drawn to illustrate.
strings: The Texas Department of Transportation launched the first phase of Project Nexus at Fort Worth Alliance Airport, as part of a federal pilot program for new aircraft. The FAA called it the first Texas demonstration under the program. The tower and the radio path are drawn to illustrate.

S3.headline: Two Caravans, by two companies' word
S3.body: Merlin's release pictures its Caravan at Alliance Airport. Joby said J208, a Caravan with its autonomous flight technology, would stop there on September 10th. Each release speaks for its own aircraft. Both are drawn to illustrate, unmarked.
strings: Two Caravans, by two companies' word

Merlin's release pictures its Caravan at Alliance Airport. Joby said J208, a Caravan with its autonomous flight technology, would stop there on September 10th. Each release speaks for its own aircraft. Both are drawn to illustrate, unmarked.

S4.headline: Three things Merlin says it showed
S4.body: Merlin says the demonstration, narrated by its chief executive, showed the Merlin Pilot can safely and effectively perform responsibilities traditionally managed by human pilots. Its release calls its expectations forward-looking.
strings: Three things Merlin says it showed

Merlin says the demonstration, narrated by its chief executive, showed the Merlin Pilot can safely and effectively perform responsibilities traditionally managed by human pilots. Its release calls its expectations forward-looking.

S5.headline: What three releases print
S5.body: A lamp is lit where a release says it. Only Merlin's names its Caravan, in a photo caption. None of the three says whether a pilot was aboard, and none prints a measured result.
strings: A lamp is lit where a release says it. Only Merlin's names its Caravan, in a photo caption. None of the three says whether a pilot was aboard, and none prints a measured result.

S6.headline: Phase one flies traditional aircraft
S6.body: TxDOT says the first phase tests helicopters and fixed-wing planes across the state, and that its first flights carry no passengers. The flights collect data and validate routes.
strings: TxDOT says the first phase tests helicopters and fixed-wing planes across the state, and that its first flights carry no passengers. The flights collect data and validate routes.

S7.headline: Dallas, Austin, San Antonio, then Houston
S7.body: The FAA's selection names Archer, BETA, Joby and Wisk as the Texas project's partners, and Merlin is not among them. It says they will support regional flights connecting Dallas, Austin and San Antonio, and eventually Houston.
strings: Dallas, Austin, San Antonio, then Houston

The FAA's selection names Archer, BETA, Joby and Wisk as the Texas project's partners, and Merlin is not among them. It says they will support regional flights connecting Dallas, Austin and San Antonio, and eventually Houston.

S8.headline: One of eight
S8.body: The FAA picked eight projects across 26 states from more than 30 proposals, and says the Texas kickoff made Texas the sixth place to launch. It will use the data to write new rules. Each stripe is one project, drawn to illustrate.
strings: The FAA picked eight projects across 26 states from more than 30 proposals, and says the Texas kickoff made Texas the sixth place to launch. It will use the data to write new rules. Each stripe is one project, drawn to illustrate.

S9.headline: 28 days into the three years
S9.body: TxDOT says the pilot runs in phases over three years, with passengers last. Counted from September 10th, 28 of 1,096 days had passed by October 8th. More test flights were planned through the rest of the year. None of the three releases says whether a pilot was aboard at the kickoff.
